Maya (CSM): Quick weekly check-in for Atlas Health — month-to-date hosted API expenditure vs their committed credits looks elevated. Flagged an unexpected token surge overnight. Summary below.

Maya (CSM): Snapshot (MTD):
```
MTD usage: 1.28M tokens
Committed: 1.00M tokens
Overage: 280k (+28%)
Peak QPS: 48
5xx rate: 0.4%
P50 latency: 180ms
```

billing-bot: :warning: Alert: ANOMALY detected for account `atlas-health` — sudden token ramp between 2026-03-18 02:00-04:00 UTC. Predicted monthly overage: $1.9k. See /alerts/210987 for details.

Omar (CS Ops): Saw the alert. Quick glance at routes — their continuous batching config appears to have been toggled to `off` for the chatgen route around 02:45 UTC. Reaching out to their dev.

Jules (AE): Heads-up — renewal touchpoint next Tue. If this becomes a recurring pattern we should surface it in the renewal plan.

Maya (CSM): Eve (Atlas product) — did you deploy any experiments or traffic shifts overnight?

Eve (Atlas product): Yeah, we launched an A/B on the new chat-gen model at 03:00 and accidentally left it at 5% for prod. Should've been 0.5% in staging. My bad :grimacing:. No batching change intended from our side.

Maya (CSM): That explains the spike. Can you rollback traffic to 0.5% and re-enable client-side batching? That should drop token throughput.

Eve (Atlas product): Rolling back now — switching traffic and toggling batching. Will ping when done (ETA ~10m).

Maya (CSM): Thanks. Jules — suggest we add a short-term spend guard (soft limit) at 1.1M tokens and enable email + slack alerts to CSM/AE if threshold reached.

Jules (AE): Agreed. Also please prepare a brief note for the renewal deck showing this one-off experiment risk and recommended guard rails.

Maya (CSM): Created issue CS-4321 in the ops backlog and linked the alert: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/CS-4321 — assigned to Omar, priority P2.

Omar (CS Ops): Adding a temporary circuit-breaker on their hosted route for next 24h (threshold = 1.1M tokens MTD). I'll also add a small autoscaling cap so we avoid runaway cost. Monitoring logs now.

billing-bot: Follow-up: Overage projection updated after rollback — projected incremental overage now $320 for the current billing cycle.

Maya (CSM): Great — action items: (1) Eve to confirm rollback complete (2) Omar to monitor & keep circuit-breaker live for 24h (3) Jules to draft renewal note. I'll re-run MTD numbers tomorrow AM and post an updated snapshot. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

Eve (Atlas product): Rollback complete. Back to 0.5% and batching re-enabled. Seeing QPS drop back to baseline.

Omar (CS Ops): Verified — traffic and token rate within expected band. Will keep an eye on variance alerts.

Maya (CSM): Closing loop here. I'll follow up with a short summary for the account health dashboard and add the experiment to the recommended onboarding checklist so we avoid accidental prod ramps.

Jules (AE): Thanks — useful to call this out in renewal prep.

billing-bot: Note: If further experiments planned, recommend pre-warm quota change requests to avoid throttles or unexpected autoscaling costs.

Maya (CSM): Noted. End of thread.
